items.title: The recorded searches returned no records
items.whyItMatters: Nothing was retrieved, so nothing was appraised; the leads are unchecked and two are undated, so no certainty can be claimed.
items.opportunity: Retrieve and check the leads by identifier before citing any, and let the trial answer the local question.

items.title: Trigger criteria have not been checked against local data
items.whyItMatters: The number of patients meeting a trigger drives both power and palliative care workload, and it is not known.
items.opportunity: Run the trigger rules silently on 2025 records to count eligible patients per clinic and month before the first step.

items.title: Palliative care clinic capacity
items.whyItMatters: About 30 new patients a week is the ceiling; if triggers add more, waits rise for everyone referred.
items.opportunity: Switch clinics in pairs, monitor waiting time monthly, and let an oversight group slow the rollout.

items.title: Patients an automatic referral may miss or distress
items.whyItMatters: Patients far from the centre, patients who need an interpreter and patients from communities where palliative care is linked with giving up may respond differently to an unrequested call.
items.opportunity: Use interpreters and telehealth, record declines with reasons, and report results by distance, language and area deprivation.

items.title: An earlier first visit is a process, not the benefit
items.whyItMatters: Counting earlier visits as success could hide no change for patients.
items.opportunity: Make days alive and out of hospital the primary outcome and keep the first visit as a process measure.

errorsFound: The scan reply rated certainty moderate over a search that returned no records; the rating was dropped and certainty stays unassessed.
The need counts an earlier first palliative care visit as the benefit; it is a process step, and the benefit to patients needs its own outcome.
reevaluation: With nothing retrieved, the gaps favour a trial that measures patient-centred outcomes from routine data, checks the trigger volume first, and treats capacity as a balancing measure.
summary: Five gaps; the empty searches, the unknown trigger volume and clinic capacity are high severity.
